meta.title: Govern Me Harder, Daddy!
meta.logline: Mayor Hart makes everything in Kindleton free and taxes everyone at one hundred and ten percent, and Penny's lemonade stand goes bankrupt in one afternoon.
meta.focus: Book chapter 7: the welfare and nanny state as suicidal empathy, punishing taxes, 'nominally free' healthcare.
meta.source: Ideas from 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), plus published criticism of the book (The Bulwark, Quillette).
meta.disclaimer: Parody and commentary for adults. Strong language. Original characters. Not affiliated with any author, network or show.

ken.name: Ken Brightside
ken.role: News anchor whose contractual grin hides a seething void

mayor.name: Mayor Marigold Hart
mayor.role: Feelings-first mayor; if it feels good, it's law

dale.name: Dale Doormat
dale.role: Dad who physically cannot say no

penny.name: Penny Doormat
penny.role: 12-year-old skeptic and the only adult in the house

bounds.name: Dr. Hal Bounds
bounds.role: Divorced evolutionary behavioral scientist; carries the book's thesis

kindt.name: Dr. Iris Kindt

rocco.name: Rocco
rocco.role: A raccoon who has never once heard the word no

lines.text: Mayor Hart has made everything in Kindleton free. Free food, free housing, free healthcare.
To pay for it, taxes are now one hundred and ten percent. Yes, folks. You now owe money for earning money.

sequence.ticker: FREE LUNCH NOW MANDATORY • LUNCH TAX ALSO MANDATORY • ACCOUNTANTS SEEN WEEPING IN PUBLIC

lines.text: Citizens! Nobody in Kindleton should ever have to pay for anything!
Someone always pays. Usually the person who didn't vote for it.
That's capitalist talk, Penny. Have a free lollipop. That'll be forty dollars in tax.
Great news, Penny! Your lemonade stand made twelve dollars today!
And?
The town took fourteen.
I have been taxed into debt by a lemon.
*sympathetic chitter* (hands Penny an invoice)
Kindleton General announced free healthcare for all. The waiting list for a broken leg is now fourteen years. Doctors recommend growing a new leg in the meantime.
Saad describes tax day. Two boxes on his bank page, two very large numbers, press send, and a career's savings vanish. Then he waits months to see a specialist. Nominally free, he calls it.
His broader claim: the welfare state and the nanny state are suicidal empathy turned into policy. Compassion on the brochure. Bill on the doormat. Sorry, Dale.
And the people who build stuff just leave.
Then there's his home province, Quebec, with an actual language police that measures shop signs, so the French is bigger than the English. Funded by you, naturally.
Kindleton's new Office of Kind Language has fined Penny's lemonade stand, because the word LEMONADE was bigger than the word KINDNESS. The fine is also free. Plus tax.
Kindleton's richest inventor has moved to Grimsby, along with his factory, his jobs, and his taxes. He left a note. It says, L O L.
lines.ticker: INVENTOR MOVES TO GRIMSBY • TAKES FACTORY, JOBS, AND THE GOOD BAGELS

sequence.ticker: INVENTOR MOVES TO GRIMSBY • TAKES FACTORY, JOBS, AND THE GOOD BAGELS

lines.text: Everything's free, Rocco, and I've never been this broke. My beer is free. The beer tax is nine dollars.
*knowing chitter* (orders two more on Dale's tab)
Tonight on Heart versus Head: who pays for kindness? Spoiler, it's you. It's always you.
Hal, safety nets aren't suicide. Nobody in Canada goes bankrupt because they got cancer. In plenty of places, people do.
A safety net, yes. A hammock that strangles the people holding it up, no.
And the rich will leave is the oldest threat in the book. Some do. Most stay where the customers are.
Fair. Then let's argue about the rate, not pretend the rate doesn't matter.
Help people. And count the cost.
Compassion, with a calculator.
Both guests' appearance fees have been taxed at one hundred and ten percent. They now owe us money. Thank you for coming.
New budget. A safety net for people who fall. Not a hammock for the mayor's friends. And taxes low enough that people still bother to make lemonade.
But then how will people know I care?
By whether things work.
Ugh. That's so much harder.
*officious chitter* (presents Dale with a bill for emotional support)
Rocco. Did you just tax me?
He's been on your payroll for six episodes, Dad.

sequence.title: Kindness, with a brain.
